record_title: Exact parametrization of deficient-perfect numbers of the form 2^a p q
scientific_context: For n=2^a p q with p<q odd primes, deficient-perfectness is equivalent to one of two explicit divisor parametrizations. The deficiency is necessarily either 2^e or 2^e p and can never be divisible by q, yielding an exact finite enumeration for each fixed a.
limitations: The odd part is assumed squarefree, so the theorem does not classify 2^a p^b q^c with b>1 or c>1, nor numbers with four or more distinct prime factors. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the main residual risk is equivalent coverage under older divisor-sum terminology. The 2013 paper's relevant scope was confirmed from its abstract and the subsequent 2014 primary-paper summary, but its full article text was not directly inspected. The finite verification supports but does not replace the proof; no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer enumeration from the theorem and a direct definition-based cross-check for small fixed exponents.
Deterministic output of the finite verification and initial exact cases.
